vit-dam-ghem-ha-noi.name: Hanoi Duck with Fermented Rice-Vinegar Broth and Fresh Herbs
aliases: Hanoi duck with sour rice-vinegar broth
Duck and herb platter with fermented rice vinegar
vit-dam-ghem-ha-noi.serving_basis: A shared platter of duck, vermicelli and herb garnishes for four people.
vit-dam-ghem-ha-noi.description: Hanoi duck and herb platter pairs poached duck, pork belly, omelet and Vietnamese pork roll with a galangal and fermented rice-vinegar broth, banana blossom, bean sprouts and herbs. This home version keeps the broth bright and the fresh garnishes crisp.
vit-dam-ghem-ha-noi.finished_dish: The duck is tender but intact; the broth is lightly sour with fermented rice vinegar and fragrant galangal; the fresh garnishes stay crisp.
vit-dam-ghem-ha-noi.serving: Arrange the duck, pork belly, omelet and pork roll with vermicelli, banana blossom, bean sprouts, herbs and pickled shallots. Ladle hot broth into bowls; add a little lime shrimp paste dip if desired.
tips: Briefly blanch the duck and bones, then rinse the pot for a clearer, cleaner broth.
Add fermented rice vinegar near the end and adjust gradually because its acidity varies by batch.
Keep raw poultry away from ready-to-eat garnishes; chill leftovers within two hours.
search_terms: Hanoi duck with fermented rice-vinegar broth
duck with banana blossom and fresh herbs
vit-dam-ghem-ha-noi.image_alt: A Hanoi platter of sliced duck, vermicelli, banana blossom and fresh herbs with a bowl of galangal broth.
vit-dam-ghem-ha-noi.time_note: About 130 minutes including a 15-minute seasoning rest; simmering time depends on the duck pieces.

preparation_steps.instruction: Rinse the duck and pat it dry. Season with half the fish sauce, salt and bruised galangal for 15 minutes. Blanch the pork bones and duck for 2 minutes, discard the water, then rinse the meat and pot.
Poach the pork belly separately until just cooked; cool and slice. Make a thin omelet, then slice it and the pork roll into strips. Soak the dried shrimp until softened.
Prepare and drain the banana blossom, sprouts and herbs, keeping them separate. Blanch the vermicelli according to its package directions and drain.

cooking_steps.instruction: Add the pork bones, dried shrimp and 2.2 litres water to a pot. Bring to a boil, lower the heat and simmer for 35 minutes, skimming as needed. Add the duck and remaining galangal; simmer until tender and the thickest pieces reach at least 74°C, about 35–45 minutes depending on size.

Transfer the duck to a clean plate and strain the broth. Add fermented rice vinegar, remaining fish sauce and sugar; adjust to a gently sour, balanced taste. Bring the broth back to a boil, then keep it hot.

Cut or slice the duck into serving pieces. Arrange it with the pork belly, omelet and pork roll beside the vermicelli, fresh garnishes and pickled shallots. Ladle over hot broth at the table; serve the optional lime shrimp paste separately.

vit-hap-hoa-sen-non-lien-ap.name: Hanoi-Style Duck Steamed with Young Lotus Buds
aliases: Duck steamed with young lotus buds
vit-hap-hoa-sen-non-lien-ap.serving_basis: Chopped duck steamed with young lotus buds as a main dish for four.
vit-hap-hoa-sen-non-lien-ap.description: This duck preparation steamed with young lotus buds appears in Tan Da thuc pham (1943). The recorded method lightly seasons chopped duck with fish sauce and salt, then steams it over the buds for more than an hour. This home adaptation keeps the seasoning restrained so the softened lotus can be eaten with the duck.
vit-hap-hoa-sen-non-lien-ap.finished_dish: The duck is tender with a delicate lotus aroma; the buds are soft, gently sweet and still hold their shape.
vit-hap-hoa-sen-non-lien-ap.serving: Arrange the cooked lotus buds as a bed and place the hot duck on top. Serve with plain rice or wrap the duck in young lotus leaf and dip in mild ginger fish sauce.
tips: Choose closed, young lotus buds without bruises; rinse carefully and drain before steaming.
Keep the seasoning light to preserve the lotus aroma; bring the steamer water to a boil first.
Use a food thermometer to check that the thickest piece reaches at least 74°C; do not let the steamer run dry.
vit-hap-hoa-sen-non-lien-ap.image_alt: Chopped duck steamed over young lotus buds and served on a simple ceramic platter.
vit-hap-hoa-sen-non-lien-ap.time_note: About 105 minutes including a 10-minute seasoning rest; steaming takes over an hour depending on piece size.

preparation_steps.instruction: Pat the duck dry with paper towels, check for any remaining pin feathers and cut into pieces. Season with fish sauce and salt for 10 minutes, keeping it separate from ready-to-eat ingredients.
Gently rinse each lotus bud, remove any bruised outer petals and drain. Line the steamer with young lotus leaves if using; prepare a covered steamer.

cooking_steps.instruction: Bring the water in a steamer to a boil. Arrange the lotus buds in the steamer basket, set the duck on top and cover tightly.

Steam over medium heat for 65–75 minutes, adding boiling water if needed. Turn the larger pieces once after about 40 minutes; check that the thickest part reaches at least 74°C and the meat is tender.
Transfer the duck to a clean platter and arrange the softened buds underneath or around it. Rest for 5 minutes and serve hot.

vit-hap-hoa-sen-non-lien-ap.media_alt_text: Steamed duck pieces arranged on a young lotus bud and served on a simple ceramic plate.

ga-nuong-song-cau-phu-yen.name: Song Cau Grilled Chicken, Phu Yen
ga-nuong-song-cau-phu-yen.serving_basis: One butterflied free-range chicken with a dipping salt for four people.
ga-nuong-song-cau-phu-yen.description: Song Cau grilled chicken is recognized as a specialty associated with Song Cau, Phu Yen. Bếp Việt butterflies a free-range chicken, seasons it with fish sauce, onion, garlic and pepper, then grills it slowly for browned skin and juicy meat. The home seasoning and timing are editorial and do not represent one restaurant's recipe.
ga-nuong-song-cau-phu-yen.finished_dish: The skin is golden brown with a few fragrant charred spots; the meat is cooked through, juicy and moderately seasoned.
ga-nuong-song-cau-phu-yen.serving: Carve the chicken into pieces and serve hot with lime-pepper salt, fresh greens and plain rice or sticky rice.
tips: Butterfly and press the chicken flat for even heat; pat the skin dry before seasoning.
Grill on a rack over a tray so fat does not drip into the flame.
Check the thickest part of the thigh for at least 74°C; rest the chicken for 10 minutes before carving.
ga-nuong-song-cau-phu-yen.image_alt: A whole golden butterflied chicken grilled in the Song Cau style of Phu Yen, served on a platter.
ga-nuong-song-cau-phu-yen.time_note: About 95 minutes including a 30-minute marinade; grilling time depends on the oven, grill and chicken weight.

preparation_steps.instruction: Clean the chicken, pat it dry and butterfly it along the breastbone. Press it flat and make shallow cuts in the thick thighs so the seasoning can penetrate.
Mix the fish sauce, shallots, garlic, onion, sugar, pepper, oil and chili if using. Rub over both sides and marinate in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Wash the greens and mix the lime-pepper salt. Heat the oven to 200°C or prepare a grill with a moderate-heat zone.

cooking_steps.instruction: Place the chicken on a rack over a drip tray. Roast at 200°C or grill over moderate heat for about 45–60 minutes, turning once; lower the heat or loosely cover with foil if the skin darkens too quickly.
Check that the thickest part of the thigh reaches at least 74°C; a larger bird may need more time. Do not brush on marinade that has touched raw chicken.
Transfer the chicken to a clean platter and rest for 10 minutes before carving. Serve hot with greens, rice and lime-pepper salt.

ga-nuong-song-cau-phu-yen.media_alt_text: Golden grilled free-range chicken, butterflied in Song Cau style and served whole on a platter.

bun-ngan-tron-chua-ngot-ha-noi.name: Hanoi Sweet-and-Sour Duck Vermicelli
bun-ngan-tron-chua-ngot-ha-noi.serving_basis: Rice vermicelli tossed with Muscovy duck, sour bamboo shoots, peanuts and herbs for four.
bun-ngan-tron-chua-ngot-ha-noi.description: Sweet-and-sour duck vermicelli is a Hanoi-style meal of rice noodles and sliced duck tossed with sour bamboo shoots, Vietnamese mint, peanuts and a sweet-sour dressing, with broth on the side. Bếp Việt cooks the duck and offal thoroughly and tosses the noodles just before serving.
bun-ngan-tron-chua-ngot-ha-noi.finished_dish: Loose vermicelli is lightly coated in a balanced sweet-sour dressing; the duck is firm and juicy, bamboo shoots crisp, and herbs and peanuts fresh.
bun-ngan-tron-chua-ngot-ha-noi.serving: Toss the vermicelli with just enough dressing. Top with duck, gizzard, liver, sour bamboo shoots and herbs; finish with peanuts and fried shallots. Serve at once with hot broth.
tips: Blanch and taste the sour bamboo shoots first; if too salty or sharp, boil and rinse them.
Poach the duck gently and skim the broth; check that both meat and offal reach at least 74°C.
Keep dressing away from raw duck and toss the noodles just before serving so they do not soften.
dish_type: Mixed vermicelli with broth on the side

bun-ngan-tron-chua-ngot-ha-noi.time_note: About 115 minutes including a 20-minute rest; the duck can be poached ahead and noodles tossed when serving.

preparation_steps.instruction: Pat the duck dry with paper towels and check for remaining pin feathers. Lightly season with 15 ml fish sauce and half the salt; refrigerate while preparing other ingredients.
Taste the sour bamboo shoots; blanch for 2–3 minutes and rinse if too salty or sharp. Wash and drain the herbs; roast peanuts if needed.
Mix the dressing with 25 ml of the fish sauce reserved for it, lime juice, sugar, 120 ml water, garlic and chili. Adjust to a gentle sweet-sour balance and keep it away from raw duck.

cooking_steps.instruction: Add the duck, ginger, shallots, 15 ml fish sauce reserved for the broth and 2.5 litres water to a pot. Bring to a boil, skim, then lower the heat and simmer until tender and the thickest thigh reaches at least 74°C, about 50–60 minutes.

Transfer the duck to a clean platter and rest for 20 minutes before removing the bones and slicing. Poach the gizzards and liver until fully cooked and at least 74°C; transfer to a clean plate and slice. Season the broth with the remaining salt, simmer the sour bamboo shoots in it for 5 minutes, then reserve them for topping.

Blanch the vermicelli according to its package directions and drain. Divide among bowls, add just enough dressing, then top with duck, gizzard, liver, bamboo shoots and herbs. Finish with peanuts, fried shallots and scallions. Serve hot broth on the side.

cha-ngong-nuong.name: Grilled Vietnamese Goose Patties
cha-ngong-nuong.serving_basis: About twelve grilled goose patties, serving four people.
cha-ngong-nuong.description: Vietnamese cha ngong nuong uses minced goose breast or thigh with a little fat to keep the patties tender. Lemongrass, garlic, shallot, pepper and honey brown fragrant on the grill. Bếp Việt's home recipe uses a thermometer to make sure the minced poultry cooks safely throughout.
cha-ngong-nuong.finished_dish: The patties are golden brown with lightly charred fragrant edges; the inside is moist, cohesive and fully cooked, with lemongrass and garlic aromas.
cha-ngong-nuong.serving: Serve the patties hot on skewers with fresh herbs, cucumber, rice or vermicelli. Offer lime-pepper salt or sweet-sour fish sauce for dipping.
tips: Choose goose thigh or breast with a little fat; mince it to a coarse paste so the patties stay juicy.
Rest the mixture in the refrigerator for 30 minutes so it binds and absorbs the seasoning.
Grill until the center of each patty reaches at least 74°C; do not rely on surface color alone.
cha-ngong-nuong.image_alt: Golden grilled goose patties on skewers served with fresh herbs, cucumber and lime-pepper salt.
cha-ngong-nuong.time_note: About 75 minutes including a 30-minute chilled rest; grilling time varies with patty size and equipment.

preparation_steps.instruction: Coarsely mince the goose and fat. Finely mince the lemongrass, shallots and garlic; keep the raw-meat board, knife and bowl away from ready-to-eat herbs.
Mix the meat with lemongrass, shallots, garlic, honey, salt, pepper and annatto oil. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Moisten your hands and shape the mixture into about twelve patties, each 2 cm thick. Thread onto skewers if desired; heat an oven or grill to medium-high.

cooking_steps.instruction: Place the patties on a rack over a drip tray. Roast at 200°C or grill over moderate charcoal, turning often so they cook evenly without burning the honey.
Grill for about 12–18 minutes depending on size. Use a thermometer to check that the center of the thickest patties reaches at least 74°C; continue cooking if needed.
Transfer the patties to a clean platter and rest for 3 minutes. Serve hot with herbs, cucumber and lime-pepper salt.
